facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Revenue has not fallen far (USD 40,650 million in FY2024, USD 45,426 million in FY2025 and USD 44,127 million over the last twelve months), so the damage is margin. The medical care ratio, medical costs as a share of premium revenue, was 92.1% for the nine months of 2026 against 90.8% a year earlier and 89.1% in FY2024. Because EBITDA is a thin residual of USD 41,588 million of last-twelve-months premium revenue, an increase of 0.80 percentage points in that ratio with premiums unchanged would remove all of it, and each percentage point is worth USD 415.88 million (an analyst sensitivity, not an issuer figure). Creditors therefore carry one cost-trend ratio that state rate-setting, not the company, largely controls. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Cash generation improved in 2026 for reasons other than earnings. Operating cash flow was USD 629 million for the nine months against an outflow of USD 237 million a year earlier, yet net income fell to USD 112 million from USD 632 million: working-capital movements turned from an outflow of USD 1,082 million to an inflow of USD 297 million, and the issuer attributes this mainly to smaller settlements with government agencies (USD 185 million paid against USD 467 million). The inflow came early: operating cash flow was USD 1,082 million in the first quarter, then an outflow of USD 294 million in the second and USD 159 million in the third, and cash and cash equivalents fell from USD 5,314 million at 2026-03-31 to USD 4,479 million at 2026-09-30. FY2025 operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 535 million (working capital an outflow of USD 1,289 million) and free cash flow after USD 101 million of capital spending an outflow of USD 636 million. Financing outflows of USD 31 million in 2026 were only stock withheld for taxes and other items, so no shares were repurchased, whereas USD 1,000 million was bought in the first nine months of 2025, which removes the biggest discretionary outflow of 2025. facts.text: The strongest contrary evidence is that the weakest quarter is about to leave the last-twelve-months window. EBITDA for the fourth quarter of 2025, calculated as FY2025 less the nine months, was an outflow of USD 118 million against USD 122 million, USD 185 million and USD 144 million in the first three quarters of 2026, and 2026 guidance implies fourth-quarter 2026 net income of roughly USD 10 million at its minimum against a loss of USD 160 million a year earlier, so last-twelve-months EBITDA should rise at the next report even though the new Florida contract is guided to cost USD 1.50 per share in that quarter. The USD 93 million impairment in the first quarter also depresses the period: before it, last-twelve-months EBITDA would be USD 426 million and EBITDA over accrued interest 2.00x. No note matures before 2028, the USD 1,250 million revolver is undrawn, the securities class action was dismissed with prejudice on 2026-10-20, and the issuer states that every covenant was met at 2026-09-30. - EBITDA is not printed in any source, so every leverage and cover ratio rests on a constructed denominator and the issuer's own adjusted measures cannot be matched to it. Severity High. Obtain the credit agreement's definition of consolidated EBITDA. - Cash interest paid for the nine months of 2026 and 2025 is not printed, so the last-twelve-months cash interest cover is not calculable and the accrued-interest cover is used as a labelled substitute. Severity Medium. Obtain the interim cash flow supplemental disclosure or a lender notice. - Income taxes paid for the interim periods are not printed. Severity Low. No ratio depends on it. - The revolver size at 2024-12-31 under the prior credit agreement is not printed in the supplied documents, so undrawn committed facilities for FY2024 are not supplied. Severity Low. Supply the 2024 annual report. - Letters of credit issued under the revolver are not printed; available capacity equals the full commitment, which implies none. Severity Low. Confirm with the lender compliance notice. - The FY2023 balance sheet is not in the supplied documents, so FY2023 debt, net debt and leverage are not supplied. Severity Low. Supply the 2023 annual report. - The legal rank and security of the revolver and of the finance leases are not stated in the filings, so they are left out of the debt stack. Severity Medium. Supply the credit agreement. - The covenant definitions are in the credit agreement, which is not supplied, so no ratio or headroom is calculated. Severity High. Supply the agreement and its first amendment. - The income statement and cash flow statements print dashes where no amount arose, such as the impairment line in the comparative periods, business combinations and borrowings in 2026, the senior notes proceeds line in the quarterly reports, and the Other segment amounts in some periods; each is shown as not supplied rather than zero, and the printed totals tie without them. Severity Low. No action. - The current portion of finance lease liabilities and the operating lease liabilities are printed only in the annual report, so lease claims at 2026-09-30 are incomplete. Severity Low. Supply the lease note when the next annual report is available. - No fourth-quarter 2025 release is supplied, so FY2025 cannot be reconciled to the sum of its quarters and the fourth quarter is derived by difference. Severity Low. Supply the earnings release for the fourth quarter of 2025. - Parent-only statements are annual, and the nine-month 2025 comparatives for dividends and capital contributions at the parent are not printed in the quarterly report. Severity Medium. Obtain parent-only interim statements. - Quarterly cash flow statements are cumulative and the third quarter alone is not printed, so the third quarter columns exist only in the income statement. Severity Low. No action. - Subsidiary minimum capital and surplus is printed in billions to one decimal only, so the dashboard states it as not supplied in millions. Severity Low. Supply statutory filings.

facts.label: Bottom line
facts.text: Creditor risk comes from the business and its capital returns, not from a sponsor: Molina is a listed pure-play government managed-care operator with no controlling holder disclosed, and we assign medium sponsor and governance risk. Medicaid is 74.89% of premium revenue, three states each supply about 10% or more, and the state contracts run three to five years and can be ended by either side, so revenue visibility is moderate. Membership has fallen 11.46% since year-end. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The operating model turns on one ratio the company does not set. Premiums are fixed per member by each state and must be actuarially sound, while the company bears medical cost risk, so cost trend above rate updates lifts the medical care ratio: 92.1% for the nine months of 2026 against 90.8% a year earlier. The reported ratio flatters the trend, because favourable reserve releases of USD 352 million helped it; on current-year costs alone the ratio was 93.22% against 91.15%. With last-twelve-months premium revenue of USD 41,588 million, each percentage point of the ratio is worth USD 415.88 million of earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Capital allocation favoured buybacks in a year of heavy borrowing and falling earnings, and has since reversed. Share purchases of USD 500 million in the first quarter of 2025 came at an average of USD 297.83 a share and USD 500 million in the third quarter at USD 175.50, in a year when the company also borrowed USD 650 million in the first quarter and USD 1,100 million over the first nine months; the filings do not link the two. Acquisitions were modest by comparison: ConnectiCare for USD 350 million of cash. In FY2025 the parent's buybacks (USD 1,000 million), the acquisition (USD 350 million) and subsidiary contributions (USD 439 million) came to USD 1,789 million against USD 1,823 million of subsidiary dividends and net note proceeds, which left little over for its other outflows, and its cash and investments ended at USD 223 million. In 2026 the company stopped repurchasing, which is creditor-aligned, but an amendment on 2026-02-04 cut the minimum interest cover test to 1.75x for the rest of 2026 for reasons the filings do not give. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is that nothing here shows value moved to owners at creditors' expense beyond buybacks, and that the buybacks have stopped. Regulated subsidiaries paid USD 985 million of dividends to the parent in FY2025 out of cash above their capital needs, parent cash and investments rose to USD 608 million, the notes were termed out to 2031, and the revolver is undrawn. Management also says it has won 90% of Medicaid re-procurements and 80% of new contracts since 2019, which is its own characterisation and cannot be tested here. The view would improve if buybacks stay suspended after the authority lapses on 2026-12-31 and the medical care ratio falls back toward its FY2025 level of 91.7%. It would worsen if purchases resume while the ratio is above its FY2025 level, if a large-state contract is lost, or if the proxy statement shows a holder with control and a distribution appetite. facts.text: There is no sponsor transaction. The only acquisition in the period was ConnectiCare, bought for USD 350 million of cash and closed on 2025-02-01.

facts.label: Bottom line
facts.text: Molina's fundamental credit is weak at present because earnings no longer cover its leverage: last-twelve-months EBITDA of USD 333 million against USD 3,771 million of parent notes is 11.32x, though near-term liquidity and a first maturity in 2028 give noteholders time. The main downside path is medical cost trend outrunning premium rates while membership shrinks: an increase of 0.80 percentage points in the medical care ratio, with premiums unchanged, would remove all last-twelve-months EBITDA, and the USD 352 million of favourable reserve development that helped 2026 cannot be assumed to recur. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C5; calculation C6

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Earnings, not debt, are the weak link. EBITDA built by Financial foundation fell from USD 1,893 million in FY2024 to USD 976 million in FY2025 and USD 333 million over the last twelve months, while revenue was USD 40,650 million, USD 45,426 million and USD 44,127 million, so the damage is margin. The medical care ratio rose to 92.1% for the nine months of 2026 from 90.8%, the Medicaid ratio to 92.6% from 91.2%, and on current-year costs alone to 93.22% from 91.15%, because USD 352 million of favourable reserve development flattered the reported figure. State and federal premium rates are set annually, so the company cannot reprice quickly, and each percentage point of the ratio is worth USD 415.88 million of EBITDA. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 32–33; calculation C1; calculation C5; calculation C6

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Liquidity buys time but is held in the wrong place. Unrestricted cash and investments of USD 8,579 million exceed claims and government settlements owed of USD 6,129 million by only USD 2,450 million, and most of it sits in regulated plans; the parent held USD 608 million, which is USD 3,163 million less than the debt it owes. Dividends of about USD 170 million can be paid without approval, which is 88.83% of the annual coupons on the notes, so servicing them relies on regulators approving more. Net cash passed up to the parent covered its interest expense 2.84x in FY2025 but 1.24x in the first nine months of 2026. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 36, 39; calculation C3; calculation C9; calculation C10

facts.text: Refinancing is a 2028 question, not a 2026 one, but replacement debt would cost more. The first maturity is USD 800 million on 2028-06-15, followed by USD 650 million in 2030 and USD 2,350 million across 2031 to 2033, and the USD 1,250 million revolver is undrawn to 2030-11-20. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The business model concentrates risk in one program and four states. Medicaid was 74.89% of premium revenue and the Texas, California, Washington and New York contracts together 40.23%; state contracts run three to five years, can be ended by either party and are rebid, and membership at 2026-09-30 was 13.61% below a year earlier, with Marketplace down 59.24% since year-end. Management expects the federal budget law to cut premium by 2% to 3% a year through 2029, and the premium it states for the new Florida contract is hard to reconcile with its enrolment, so replacement revenue is uncertain. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a weak assessment is that the worst quarter is leaving the window. EBITDA for the fourth quarter of 2025 was an outflow of USD 118 million against USD 144 million in the third quarter of 2026, and 2026 guidance implies fourth-quarter net income of roughly USD 10 million, so last-twelve-months EBITDA should rise at the next report even though the new Florida contract is guided to cost USD 1.50 per share in that quarter. Before the USD 93 million impairment, last-twelve-months EBITDA would have been USD 426 million and EBITDA over accrued interest 2.00x. Management says medical cost trend appears to be plateauing and 2027 rate updates are strong, which is its own view and untested here. Nothing matures before 2028 and the revolver is undrawn. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-10-21_moh3q26_er.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_moh3q26_er.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation C14

facts.label: Market forces
facts.text: Buyer power is the dominant force: the buyers are state agencies and the federal government, which set rates and rebid contracts, so Molina has little pricing power and its margin depends on rate adequacy. Supplier power sits with providers and drug suppliers, where outpatient and high-cost drug categories drove the Medicaid ratio up. Rivalry takes the form of procurement competition and sector consolidation, and entry barriers are regulatory and procurement-based, so new entrants are a limited threat. Policy is the primary external driver: the federal budget law is expected to cut Medicaid enrolment gradually from 2027 and reduce premium by 2% to 3% a year through 2029, and Marketplace rule changes have shrunk that book. For creditors the sector translates into a slow-moving but one-way risk to revenue and a rate-lag risk to margin. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_moh-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 28, 33; calculation C8

facts.label: Outlook
facts.text: Over the next twelve to twenty-four months the revenue base is expected to shrink further (Medicaid to about 4.4 million members by year-end excluding the new Florida enrolment, Marketplace to about 250,000, Medicare to about 230,000) while new contracts start between 2026-10-01 and 2027-01-01, and the first-quarter 2026 impairment and the fourth-quarter 2025 loss drop out of the reported figures. Over three to five years the federal budget law reduces Medicaid expansion enrolment gradually and limits provider tax financing from 2028, and management targets premium and earnings growth of 11% to 13% that is not supported by figures in the documents. The credit implication is that deleveraging depends on margin recovery rather than debt paydown, because nothing matures before 2028 and the notes are not prepayable from free cash flow at this scale. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The initiating condition is that state rate updates for 2027 do not keep pace with medical cost trend while the favourable prior-year reserve development seen in 2026 does not repeat. The first operational break is the medical care ratio: without the USD 352 million of reserve release the nine-month EBITDA would have been USD 99 million and last-twelve-months EBITDA an outflow of USD 19 million, before any offset from minimum medical loss ratio rules and cost corridors. That feeds through subsidiary earnings to dividends: about USD 170 million can be paid without approval against annual coupons that are higher, so the parent would draw on its USD 608 million of cash, which covers about 33.99 months of accrued interest at the 2026 pace. Leverage would be undefined on a negative EBITDA and the interest cover test, already cut to 1.75x, would be the observable trigger; if it were breached the undrawn revolver could become unavailable and a covenant default under it could in turn engage the cross-default terms of the notes, although the filings do not give the definitions or thresholds. Management levers are suspending buybacks, repricing or exiting products, and capital moves between subsidiaries. Resilience looks sufficient to avoid a liquidity event in the next twelve months, because of the USD 8,579 million of unrestricted cash and investments and no maturity before 2028, but not sufficient to hold its current credit quality if the ratio keeps rising. facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: The strengths are a maturity profile with nothing due before 2028 and an undrawn revolver, which means a refinancing event is not the near-term test; low capital intensity, with capital spending of USD 101 million against USD 45,426 million of revenue; the suspension of buybacks and the rise in parent cash to USD 608 million; a record of renewing and winning state contracts, in management's words; and audited, transparent reporting that lets creditors see where the weakness is. The weaknesses are margins that depend on a ratio the company does not set and that has moved from 90.8% to 92.1% in a year; leverage of 11.32x on last-twelve-months EBITDA with accrued interest cover of 1.56x; concentration, with Medicaid at 74.89% and four states at 40.23% of premium revenue; a parent that relies on subsidiary dividends and holds a small part of group cash; and shrinking membership with policy headwinds through 2029. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Molina presents a business profile of adequate scale supported by contract-based government revenue, a maturity profile with no principal due before 2028 and low capital needs, but credit quality is constrained by margins that have collapsed with the medical care ratio, concentration in Medicaid and four states, and a parent that owes all the debt while most cash sits in regulated plans. Cash-flow durability appears weak at present because operating cash flow swings with settlement timing and reported earnings include reserve releases. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on whether the medical care ratio recovers before 2028 and on the coupon needed to replace notes now carrying low rates. The primary downside path is medical costs outrunning premium rates while membership falls. Further analysis would require the credit agreement definitions, the proxy statement, market prices of the notes and management's 2027 plan. Fundamental credit review completed with limitations. Top risk: the medical care ratio. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); calculation C2; calculation C6

## Findings
### Bottom line

The seven supplied SEC documents support the financial foundation, business profile and fundamental credit view of Molina Healthcare's senior unsecured notes, but not covenant headroom or instrument-level legal terms, because no executed credit agreement or indenture was supplied.

Readiness is therefore ready with limitations for the three analytical modules in this run, conditional for peer benchmark, ratings triggers and security selection, and blocked for legal and covenant work and market-implied risk. The latest evidence is the third-quarter 2026 report signed on 2026-10-22, before the 2026-11-05 cutoff; the main source limits are the missing covenant definitions, parent-only interim statements and governance disclosures held in a proxy statement that was not supplied.

spans.text: ## Request

Financial foundation for MOLINA HEALTHCARE, INC. (issuer id moh), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the consolidated statements in US dollars for FY2023 to FY2025 and the nine months to 2026-09-30, the debt, cash and liquidity tables, and the leverage and cover ratios built from them, with the parent-only statements used for the perimeter of the senior notes. Where the filings print no EBITDA, it is built from operating income and depreciation and amortization and labelled as calculated.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

Earnings, far more than debt, drive the credit risk: last-twelve-months EBITDA of USD 333 million against USD 3,771 million of parent senior notes is reported leverage of 11.32x, up from 1.54x at FY2024, so creditors rely on cash and distant maturities.

The group holds net cash on its balance sheet (cash of USD 4,479 million against debt of USD 3,771 million), but the notes sit at the parent, which held only about USD 608 million, while USD 6,129 million of claims and government settlements are owed out of group cash and investments.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-K_2025-12-31_moh-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 105–106; calculation C3; calculation C13; calculation C17; calculation C18

No note matures before June 2028 and the USD 1,250 million revolver is undrawn, so the near-term question is whether earnings recover, not refinancing; interest cover on the covenant definition cannot be tested because the filings do not give it.
### Key findings

Reported leverage has risen mainly because earnings fell, with new debt a smaller cause. EBITDA, which the issuer does not print and which is built here as operating income plus depreciation and amortization, fell from USD 1,893 million in FY2024 to USD 976 million in FY2025 and to USD 333 million over the last twelve months. Debt rose from USD 2,923 million at FY2024 to USD 3,771 million at 2026-09-30, USD 848 million more after the senior notes due 2031 were issued in November 2025, but holding debt at its FY2024 level would still give 8.78x on the latest EBITDA, so most of the rise to 11.32x comes from the denominator.

Basis: calculation C1; calculation C3; calculation C33; 10-K_2025-12-31_moh-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 105–106; 10-K_2025-12-31_moh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 131; 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14

Revenue has not fallen far (USD 40,650 million in FY2024, USD 45,426 million in FY2025 and USD 44,127 million over the last twelve months), so the damage is margin. The medical care ratio, medical costs as a share of premium revenue, was 92.1% for the nine months of 2026 against 90.8% a year earlier and 89.1% in FY2024. Because EBITDA is a thin residual of USD 41,588 million of last-twelve-months premium revenue, an increase of 0.80 percentage points in that ratio with premiums unchanged would remove all of it, and each percentage point is worth USD 415.88 million (an analyst sensitivity, not an issuer figure). Creditors therefore carry one cost-trend ratio that state rate-setting, not the company, largely controls.

Basis: calculation C2; calculation C10; calculation C25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-K_2025-12-31_moh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 81; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_moh3q26_er.htm.jsonl, page 1

The group reports net cash, but the claim noteholders hold is on the parent. Cash and cash equivalents of USD 4,479 million exceed the USD 3,771 million of debt by USD 708 million. The notes are obligations of the parent corporation, which held about USD 608 million of cash and investments at 2026-09-30 (USD 223 million at 2025-12-31), so parent debt exceeded parent liquid holdings by USD 3,163 million. The rest of the cash sits in regulated health plans that must hold minimum capital of about USD 3.0 billion and may pay only about USD 170 million of dividends without regulatory approval.
Basis: calculation C13; calculation C17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-K_2025-12-31_moh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 142

Much of the cash is working-capital float rather than free liquidity. Medical claims payable of USD 4,988 million and amounts due to government agencies of USD 1,141 million, together USD 6,129 million, are non-interest-bearing obligations that premium cash is held to meet. Against unrestricted cash and investments of USD 8,579 million they leave USD 2,450 million, compared with USD 2,473 million at FY2024 and USD 2,043 million at FY2025. Membership fell 11.46% over the nine months while claims payable rose, so cash would leave to settle older claims if claims payable fell in step with enrolment.

Basis: calculation C18; calculation C19; calculation C28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-K_2025-12-31_moh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 105

Interest is serviced by the parent from cash passed up by regulated subsidiaries, and that support has thinned. In FY2025 the parent received USD 985 million of dividends and contributed USD 439 million, a net USD 546 million, which was 2.84x its interest expense of USD 192 million; for the nine months of 2026 the net was USD 199 million against USD 161 million of interest, or 1.24x. The two figures are not defined identically (the quarterly report counts dividends and returns of capital) and dividends are lumpy within a year, so the comparison shows direction, not a precise change.
Basis: calculation C20; 10-K_2025-12-31_moh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 143; 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35

Cash generation improved in 2026 for reasons other than earnings. Operating cash flow was USD 629 million for the nine months against an outflow of USD 237 million a year earlier, yet net income fell to USD 112 million from USD 632 million: working-capital movements turned from an outflow of USD 1,082 million to an inflow of USD 297 million, and the issuer attributes this mainly to smaller settlements with government agencies (USD 185 million paid against USD 467 million). The inflow came early: operating cash flow was USD 1,082 million in the first quarter, then an outflow of USD 294 million in the second and USD 159 million in the third, and cash and cash equivalents fell from USD 5,314 million at 2026-03-31 to USD 4,479 million at 2026-09-30. FY2025 operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 535 million (working capital an outflow of USD 1,289 million) and free cash flow after USD 101 million of capital spending an outflow of USD 636 million. Financing outflows of USD 31 million in 2026 were only stock withheld for taxes and other items, so no shares were repurchased, whereas USD 1,000 million was bought in the first nine months of 2025, which removes the biggest discretionary outflow of 2025.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-K_2025-12-31_moh-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 106–107; EX-99.1_2026-04-22_moh1q26_er.htm.jsonl, page 5; EX-99.1_2026-07-22_moh2q26_er.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C7; calculation C9; calculation C31; calculation C32

All debt is five senior unsecured notes of the parent, with USD 3,800 million of principal and USD 3,771 million of carrying value. Principal falls due as USD 800 million in 2028, USD 650 million in 2030, USD 850 million in 2031 and USD 750 million in each of 2032 and 2033, so nothing is due in 2026 or 2027; the USD 1,250 million revolver is undrawn and ends on 2030-11-20. Finance lease liabilities of USD 179 million are carried outside debt and are excluded from every ratio; adding the USD 209 million of finance leases at FY2025 would lift leverage to 4.07x from 3.86x. No pension, retiree-medical, factoring or supplier-finance obligation is described, and management states that its other agreements hold no material non-cancelable commitments.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15; 10-K_2025-12-31_moh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 97; 10-K_2025-12-31_moh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 127; 10-K_2025-12-31_moh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 130; calculation C14; calculation C24
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest contrary evidence is that the weakest quarter is about to leave the last-twelve-months window. EBITDA for the fourth quarter of 2025, calculated as FY2025 less the nine months, was an outflow of USD 118 million against USD 122 million, USD 185 million and USD 144 million in the first three quarters of 2026, and 2026 guidance implies fourth-quarter 2026 net income of roughly USD 10 million at its minimum against a loss of USD 160 million a year earlier, so last-twelve-months EBITDA should rise at the next report even though the new Florida contract is guided to cost USD 1.50 per share in that quarter. The USD 93 million impairment in the first quarter also depresses the period: before it, last-twelve-months EBITDA would be USD 426 million and EBITDA over accrued interest 2.00x. No note matures before 2028, the USD 1,250 million revolver is undrawn, the securities class action was dismissed with prejudice on 2026-10-20, and the issuer states that every covenant was met at 2026-09-30.

Basis: calculation C26; calculation C27; calculation C30; EX-99.1_2026-04-22_moh1q26_er.htm.jsonl, page 5; EX-99.1_2026-07-22_moh2q26_er.htm.jsonl, page 5; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_moh3q26_er.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_moh3q26_er.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9

The view would improve if the medical care ratio falls back toward the FY2025 level, if parent cash and net upstream cash keep rising from the USD 608 million and USD 199 million now reported, or if the credit agreement shows that its interest cover definition adds back items that leave a wide margin over the 1.75x minimum that applies through the end of 2026. It would worsen if the ratio keeps rising, if the float of claims and government settlements unwinds faster than cash is replenished, or if parent cash falls while dividends above about USD 170 million need regulatory approval. EBITDA over accrued interest of 1.56x is not the covenant measure and must not be read as headroom.

Basis: calculation C5; calculation C12; calculation C18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-K_2025-12-31_moh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 132
### Limitations

EBITDA is constructed from operating income and depreciation and amortization because the issuer prints none; it includes investment income earned on premium cash, carries the first-quarter impairment, and will differ from any EBITDA defined in the credit agreement.
Basis: calculation C1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_moh3q26_er.htm.jsonl, page 8
Cash interest for the nine months of 2026 and 2025 is not printed, so interest cover on cash paid exists for FY2024 and FY2025 only; the latest-period cover shown uses accrued interest expense.

The balance sheet is stated at three dates, the credit agreement and indentures are not supplied, and lease liabilities for the latest date are partly unprinted, so debt-like claims outside the notes are incomplete.
Parent-only statements are annual, so the net cash passed up to the parent for 2026 rests on a quarterly report description that is defined differently from the annual figure.

- EBITDA is not printed in any source, so every leverage and cover ratio rests on a constructed denominator and the issuer's own adjusted measures cannot be matched to it. Severity High. Obtain the credit agreement's definition of consolidated EBITDA.

- Cash interest paid for the nine months of 2026 and 2025 is not printed, so the last-twelve-months cash interest cover is not calculable and the accrued-interest cover is used as a labelled substitute. Severity Medium. Obtain the interim cash flow supplemental disclosure or a lender notice.
- Income taxes paid for the interim periods are not printed. Severity Low. No ratio depends on it.

- The revolver size at 2024-12-31 under the prior credit agreement is not printed in the supplied documents, so undrawn committed facilities for FY2024 are not supplied. Severity Low. Supply the 2024 annual report.
- Letters of credit issued under the revolver are not printed; available capacity equals the full commitment, which implies none. Severity Low. Confirm with the lender compliance notice.
- The FY2023 balance sheet is not in the supplied documents, so FY2023 debt, net debt and leverage are not supplied. Severity Low. Supply the 2023 annual report.
- The legal rank and security of the revolver and of the finance leases are not stated in the filings, so they are left out of the debt stack. Severity Medium. Supply the credit agreement.
- The covenant definitions are in the credit agreement, which is not supplied, so no ratio or headroom is calculated. Severity High. Supply the agreement and its first amendment.

- The income statement and cash flow statements print dashes where no amount arose, such as the impairment line in the comparative periods, business combinations and borrowings in 2026, the senior notes proceeds line in the quarterly reports, and the Other segment amounts in some periods; each is shown as not supplied rather than zero, and the printed totals tie without them. Severity Low. No action.

- The current portion of finance lease liabilities and the operating lease liabilities are printed only in the annual report, so lease claims at 2026-09-30 are incomplete. Severity Low. Supply the lease note when the next annual report is available.

- No fourth-quarter 2025 release is supplied, so FY2025 cannot be reconciled to the sum of its quarters and the fourth quarter is derived by difference. Severity Low. Supply the earnings release for the fourth quarter of 2025.

- Parent-only statements are annual, and the nine-month 2025 comparatives for dividends and capital contributions at the parent are not printed in the quarterly report. Severity Medium. Obtain parent-only interim statements.
- Quarterly cash flow statements are cumulative and the third quarter alone is not printed, so the third quarter columns exist only in the income statement. Severity Low. No action.
- Subsidiary minimum capital and surplus is printed in billions to one decimal only, so the dashboard states it as not supplied in millions. Severity Low. Supply statutory filings.

spans.text: ## Request

Business, transaction, ownership and governance fact pack for MOLINA HEALTHCARE, INC. (issuer id moh), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is what the issuer does, who owns and controls it, which transactions and events shape its credit, and whether governance or capital allocation raises creditor risk. The company is a listed public corporation with no sponsor, so the sponsor-behaviour work is applied to the public-company equivalents of distributions, acquisitions and refinancings.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

Creditor risk comes from the business and its capital returns, not from a sponsor: Molina is a listed pure-play government managed-care operator with no controlling holder disclosed, and we assign medium sponsor and governance risk.

Medicaid is 74.89% of premium revenue, three states each supply about 10% or more, and the state contracts run three to five years and can be ended by either side, so revenue visibility is moderate. Membership has fallen 11.46% since year-end.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_moh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_moh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_moh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 121; 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation C1; calculation C4

The parent bought back USD 1,000 million of stock in each of 2024 and 2025, equal to 211.86% of FY2025 net income, while borrowing USD 1,100 million in the first nine months of 2025. Nothing was bought in 2026, but USD 500 million of authority runs to 2026-12-31, so a resumption before earnings recover is the main creditor-adverse event to watch.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_moh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 135; 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; calculation C6; calculation C7
### Key findings

There is no sponsor to model, and that cuts both ways. Fourteen registered holders of record (including the depository nominee) hold the common stock, which is listed on the New York Stock Exchange, no cash dividend has ever been paid, and the supplied documents disclose no controlling holder, fee arrangement or related-party payment, so extraction by an owner is not evidenced. The same absence means no sponsor equity stands behind the notes: the parent's own USD 608 million of cash and investments at 2026-09-30 is the only identified buffer, and ownership percentages and board independence are held in a proxy statement that was not supplied.

Revenue is concentrated in one program and four states, and the contract model gives it little protection. Medicaid was USD 32,240 million of FY2025 premium revenue, and the Texas, California, Washington and New York Medicaid contracts together were USD 17,320 million, or 40.23% of all premium revenue. State contracts run three to five years, can be terminated by either party with or without cause, and are rebid; the Virginia contracts ended on 2025-06-30 after Molina was not an awardee. A loss of any large state contract would remove revenue that fixed costs and USD 3,771 million of parent debt service rely on.

The operating model turns on one ratio the company does not set. Premiums are fixed per member by each state and must be actuarially sound, while the company bears medical cost risk, so cost trend above rate updates lifts the medical care ratio: 92.1% for the nine months of 2026 against 90.8% a year earlier. The reported ratio flatters the trend, because favourable reserve releases of USD 352 million helped it; on current-year costs alone the ratio was 93.22% against 91.15%. With last-twelve-months premium revenue of USD 41,588 million, each percentage point of the ratio is worth USD 415.88 million of earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_moh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; calculation C5; calculation C12

Membership and revenue are contracting while new contracts are still to arrive. Total membership at 2026-09-30 was 13.61% below the same date a year earlier, with Marketplace down 59.24% since year-end through a deliberate repricing and Medicaid down 4.29%. Management expects the 2025 federal budget law to cut Medicaid premium growth by 2% to 3% a year through 2029 and a further USD 1 billion of Marketplace premium in 2027. New Florida, Illinois and Wisconsin awards start between 2026-10-01 and 2027-01-01 and the Georgia and Texas awards slipped to late 2027 or 2028, so the timing of replacement revenue is uncertain.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 28–31; calculation C4

Capital allocation favoured buybacks in a year of heavy borrowing and falling earnings, and has since reversed. Share purchases of USD 500 million in the first quarter of 2025 came at an average of USD 297.83 a share and USD 500 million in the third quarter at USD 175.50, in a year when the company also borrowed USD 650 million in the first quarter and USD 1,100 million over the first nine months; the filings do not link the two. Acquisitions were modest by comparison: ConnectiCare for USD 350 million of cash. In FY2025 the parent's buybacks (USD 1,000 million), the acquisition (USD 350 million) and subsidiary contributions (USD 439 million) came to USD 1,789 million against USD 1,823 million of subsidiary dividends and net note proceeds, which left little over for its other outflows, and its cash and investments ended at USD 223 million. In 2026 the company stopped repurchasing, which is creditor-aligned, but an amendment on 2026-02-04 cut the minimum interest cover test to 1.75x for the rest of 2026 for reasons the filings do not give.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_moh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_moh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 123; 10-K_2025-12-31_moh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 132; 10-K_2025-12-31_moh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 135; 10-K_2025-12-31_moh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 143; 10-Q_2026-03-31_moh-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C5; calculation C7; calculation C8

Disclosure is adequate for monitoring but incomplete for covenant work. The annual accounts carry an unqualified audit opinion and a critical audit matter on the reserve for claims incurred but not paid, which was USD 3,211 million of USD 4,887 million of medical claims payable; management reported effective internal controls with the ConnectiCare business excluded from the assessment. Covenant ratios are stated as met but never printed, and the 2025 securities class action and the related shareholder derivative suit were both dismissed with prejudice in October 2026 with no loss estimate recorded.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious view is that nothing here shows value moved to owners at creditors' expense beyond buybacks, and that the buybacks have stopped. Regulated subsidiaries paid USD 985 million of dividends to the parent in FY2025 out of cash above their capital needs, parent cash and investments rose to USD 608 million, the notes were termed out to 2031, and the revolver is undrawn. Management also says it has won 90% of Medicaid re-procurements and 80% of new contracts since 2019, which is its own characterisation and cannot be tested here. The view would improve if buybacks stay suspended after the authority lapses on 2026-12-31 and the medical care ratio falls back toward its FY2025 level of 91.7%. It would worsen if purchases resume while the ratio is above its FY2025 level, if a large-state contract is lost, or if the proxy statement shows a holder with control and a distribution appetite.
### Limitations

- The proxy statement is not supplied, so holder percentages, board independence and related-party dealings are not established; the finding that no controlling holder exists would change if a large holder appears there.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_moh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 149

- The credit agreement and indentures are not supplied, so legal capacity for buybacks and other restricted payments is not established; the judgement that buybacks are a mixed signal rests on conduct, not on what the documents permit.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_moh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 132

- The premium figure for the new Florida award is hard to reconcile with its stated enrolment and with the full-year guidance, so any growth view that relies on that award is bounded by management's own description.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_moh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 81; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_moh3q26_er.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C9
- Earlier acquisitions are described only by cash paid, so no pattern of acquisition behaviour or integration record is established beyond the single ConnectiCare transaction.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_moh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 92

spans.text: ## Request

Fundamental credit synthesis for MOLINA HEALTHCARE, INC. (issuer id moh), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the issuer's overall credit profile, its strongest support and weakest dimension, the primary downside path and what to monitor, built on the financial statements, the business and governance facts and the source inventory. No rating, security recommendation, legal-capacity conclusion or portfolio sizing is given.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

Molina's fundamental credit is weak at present because earnings no longer cover its leverage: last-twelve-months EBITDA of USD 333 million against USD 3,771 million of parent notes is 11.32x, though near-term liquidity and a first maturity in 2028 give noteholders time.

The main downside path is medical cost trend outrunning premium rates while membership shrinks: an increase of 0.80 percentage points in the medical care ratio, with premiums unchanged, would remove all last-twelve-months EBITDA, and the USD 352 million of favourable reserve development that helped 2026 cannot be assumed to recur.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C5; calculation C6

Support comes from USD 8,579 million of unrestricted cash and investments, an undrawn USD 1,250 million revolver, no maturity before June 2028 and suspended buybacks, but only USD 608 million sits at the parent that owes the notes, and about USD 170 million of subsidiary dividends can be paid without regulatory approval.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; calculation C3; calculation C9
### Key findings

Earnings, not debt, are the weak link. EBITDA built by Financial foundation fell from USD 1,893 million in FY2024 to USD 976 million in FY2025 and USD 333 million over the last twelve months, while revenue was USD 40,650 million, USD 45,426 million and USD 44,127 million, so the damage is margin. The medical care ratio rose to 92.1% for the nine months of 2026 from 90.8%, the Medicaid ratio to 92.6% from 91.2%, and on current-year costs alone to 93.22% from 91.15%, because USD 352 million of favourable reserve development flattered the reported figure. State and federal premium rates are set annually, so the company cannot reprice quickly, and each percentage point of the ratio is worth USD 415.88 million of EBITDA.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 32–33; calculation C1; calculation C5; calculation C6

Liquidity buys time but is held in the wrong place. Unrestricted cash and investments of USD 8,579 million exceed claims and government settlements owed of USD 6,129 million by only USD 2,450 million, and most of it sits in regulated plans; the parent held USD 608 million, which is USD 3,163 million less than the debt it owes. Dividends of about USD 170 million can be paid without approval, which is 88.83% of the annual coupons on the notes, so servicing them relies on regulators approving more. Net cash passed up to the parent covered its interest expense 2.84x in FY2025 but 1.24x in the first nine months of 2026.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 36, 39; calculation C3; calculation C9; calculation C10

Refinancing is a 2028 question, not a 2026 one, but replacement debt would cost more. The first maturity is USD 800 million on 2028-06-15, followed by USD 650 million in 2030 and USD 2,350 million across 2031 to 2033, and the USD 1,250 million revolver is undrawn to 2030-11-20. The issuer-stated fair value of the notes is 93.84% of principal, and 86.93% for the 2032 notes; S&P rates them BB- and Moody's Ba2; replacing the 2028 notes at the coupon carried by the 2031 notes would add USD 17.00 million of annual interest.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-K_2025-12-31_moh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 94; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C13

The business model concentrates risk in one program and four states. Medicaid was 74.89% of premium revenue and the Texas, California, Washington and New York contracts together 40.23%; state contracts run three to five years, can be ended by either party and are rebid, and membership at 2026-09-30 was 13.61% below a year earlier, with Marketplace down 59.24% since year-end. Management expects the federal budget law to cut premium by 2% to 3% a year through 2029, and the premium it states for the new Florida contract is hard to reconcile with its enrolment, so replacement revenue is uncertain.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_moh-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 14–16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 28–31; calculation C8

Financial policy is a medium governance risk rather than a rating driver on its own. There is no sponsor and no dividend; the parent bought back USD 1,000 million of stock in each of 2024 and 2025, 211.86% of FY2025 net income in the latest year, in a year when it also borrowed USD 1,100 million, and nothing in 2026. The covenant interest cover test was lowered temporarily to 1.75x on 2026-02-04 for reasons not given, and headroom cannot be measured because the agreement is not supplied.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_moh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 132; 10-K_2025-12-31_moh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 135; calculation C15

Cash generation is a working-capital story, not an earnings story. Operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 535 million in FY2025 and an inflow of USD 629 million in the first nine months of 2026, of which USD 297 million came from working-capital movements; by quarter it was USD 1,082 million, then outflows of USD 294 million and USD 159 million. Capital spending of USD 101 million is small, so free cash flow follows the timing of settlements with governments rather than earnings.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; EX-99.1_2026-04-22_moh1q26_er.htm.jsonl, page 5; EX-99.1_2026-07-22_moh2q26_er.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C4
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a weak assessment is that the worst quarter is leaving the window. EBITDA for the fourth quarter of 2025 was an outflow of USD 118 million against USD 144 million in the third quarter of 2026, and 2026 guidance implies fourth-quarter net income of roughly USD 10 million, so last-twelve-months EBITDA should rise at the next report even though the new Florida contract is guided to cost USD 1.50 per share in that quarter. Before the USD 93 million impairment, last-twelve-months EBITDA would have been USD 426 million and EBITDA over accrued interest 2.00x. Management says medical cost trend appears to be plateauing and 2027 rate updates are strong, which is its own view and untested here. Nothing matures before 2028 and the revolver is undrawn.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-10-21_moh3q26_er.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_moh3q26_er.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation C14

The view would improve if the medical care ratio returns toward its FY2025 level of 91.7% without reserve releases, if parent cash keeps rising from USD 608 million, or if the credit agreement shows wide headroom under the interest cover test. It would worsen if the ratio keeps rising, if the Florida start-up costs more than guided, if buybacks resume under the USD 500 million authority that lapses on 2026-12-31, or if a large-state contract is lost.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; calculation C3; calculation C15
### Limitations

- The credit agreement and indentures are not supplied, so the covenant test cannot be applied; the view that near-term default risk is low rests on liquidity and maturities, not on measured headroom.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); 10-K_2025-12-31_moh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 132
- The 11.32x leverage figure uses a constructed EBITDA that carries the first-quarter impairment, so the weak assessment is firm in direction but its size would change under a lender-defined measure.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C14
- No peer set, market price or spread is supplied, so the weak assessment is absolute rather than relative to other high-yield issuers and no market view of the notes is tested.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)
- Management's outlook for 2027 rests on one quotation and annual guidance, so the recovery path beyond fourth-quarter 2026 is not established and the contrary evidence cannot be weighed further.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-21_moh3q26_er.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2
### Business and ownership

Molina is a pure-play manager of government-funded health plans that serves 21 states, so its cash flow depends on state and federal budgets rather than on consumers. Medicaid is 74.89% of premium revenue, Medicare 14.48% and Marketplace 10.42% in FY2025, and Medicaid has risen to 78.30% of premium for the nine months of 2026 as Marketplace shrinks. Contracts are short and terminable, which gives visibility of a few years at most and exposes revenue to rebids: the Virginia contracts ended on 2025-06-30. The consequence for creditors is that debt service capacity is only as durable as the next procurement cycle.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_moh-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 14–16; calculation C8

The issuer is a listed public corporation with no sponsor and no controlling holder disclosed; the notes are obligations of the parent only, with no subsidiary guarantor named, and the regulated subsidiaries must keep minimum capital of about USD 3.0 billion. That structure removes sponsor extraction risk but also any sponsor backstop, and it makes noteholders structurally dependent on subsidiary dividends.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39
### Revenue, margin and cash conversion

Revenue is visible only through contract terms. Premiums are fixed per member and actuarially sound by requirement, but they are re-set annually while cost trend moves continuously, which is why the ratio rose even though premium revenue for Medicaid was unchanged for the nine months. Membership is falling (down 11.46% since year-end), so premium revenue fell 4% in the third quarter.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 24, 33; calculation C8

Margins cannot be defended by cost cutting alone. Medical care costs are about 92% of premium and the G&A ratio rose to 6.8% for the nine months from 6.5% as premium fell, so operating leverage is adverse: a change of less than one percentage point in the medical care ratio equals all of last-twelve-months EBITDA. The company holds some levers, notably suspending buybacks, exiting the MAPD product and repricing Marketplace, but each shrinks revenue.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 24, 26, 30; calculation C5; calculation C6

Capital intensity is low (capital spending of USD 101 million in FY2025), so EBITDA converts to cash easily in a normal year, but the conversion has been negative in the worst periods because government settlements, tax payments and claims timing swing operating cash flow by hundreds of millions. FY2025 operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 535 million on EBITDA of USD 976 million.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C4
### Market forces

Buyer power is the dominant force: the buyers are state agencies and the federal government, which set rates and rebid contracts, so Molina has little pricing power and its margin depends on rate adequacy. Supplier power sits with providers and drug suppliers, where outpatient and high-cost drug categories drove the Medicaid ratio up. Rivalry takes the form of procurement competition and sector consolidation, and entry barriers are regulatory and procurement-based, so new entrants are a limited threat. Policy is the primary external driver: the federal budget law is expected to cut Medicaid enrolment gradually from 2027 and reduce premium by 2% to 3% a year through 2029, and Marketplace rule changes have shrunk that book. For creditors the sector translates into a slow-moving but one-way risk to revenue and a rate-lag risk to margin.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_moh-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 28, 33; calculation C8

In credit terms the strengths are scale, low capital intensity, a maturity profile with nothing due before 2028 and a record of winning state contracts; the weaknesses are thin margins, parent dependence on regulated subsidiaries, state concentration and shrinking membership; the opportunities that matter are rate updates that catch up with cost trend and new contracts in Florida, Illinois and Wisconsin; the threats are further rate lag, loss of a large-state contract and policy-driven enrolment loss.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Outlook

Over the next twelve to twenty-four months the revenue base is expected to shrink further (Medicaid to about 4.4 million members by year-end excluding the new Florida enrolment, Marketplace to about 250,000, Medicare to about 230,000) while new contracts start between 2026-10-01 and 2027-01-01, and the first-quarter 2026 impairment and the fourth-quarter 2025 loss drop out of the reported figures. Over three to five years the federal budget law reduces Medicaid expansion enrolment gradually and limits provider tax financing from 2028, and management targets premium and earnings growth of 11% to 13% that is not supported by figures in the documents. The credit implication is that deleveraging depends on margin recovery rather than debt paydown, because nothing matures before 2028 and the notes are not prepayable from free cash flow at this scale.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 28–30; 10-K_2025-12-31_moh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C14
### Downside scenario

The initiating condition is that state rate updates for 2027 do not keep pace with medical cost trend while the favourable prior-year reserve development seen in 2026 does not repeat. The first operational break is the medical care ratio: without the USD 352 million of reserve release the nine-month EBITDA would have been USD 99 million and last-twelve-months EBITDA an outflow of USD 19 million, before any offset from minimum medical loss ratio rules and cost corridors. That feeds through subsidiary earnings to dividends: about USD 170 million can be paid without approval against annual coupons that are higher, so the parent would draw on its USD 608 million of cash, which covers about 33.99 months of accrued interest at the 2026 pace. Leverage would be undefined on a negative EBITDA and the interest cover test, already cut to 1.75x, would be the observable trigger; if it were breached the undrawn revolver could become unavailable and a covenant default under it could in turn engage the cross-default terms of the notes, although the filings do not give the definitions or thresholds. Management levers are suspending buybacks, repricing or exiting products, and capital moves between subsidiaries. Resilience looks sufficient to avoid a liquidity event in the next twelve months, because of the USD 8,579 million of unrestricted cash and investments and no maturity before 2028, but not sufficient to hold its current credit quality if the ratio keeps rising.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; calculation C7; calculation C16
### Strengths and weaknesses

The strengths are a maturity profile with nothing due before 2028 and an undrawn revolver, which means a refinancing event is not the near-term test; low capital intensity, with capital spending of USD 101 million against USD 45,426 million of revenue; the suspension of buybacks and the rise in parent cash to USD 608 million; a record of renewing and winning state contracts, in management's words; and audited, transparent reporting that lets creditors see where the weakness is.

The weaknesses are margins that depend on a ratio the company does not set and that has moved from 90.8% to 92.1% in a year; leverage of 11.32x on last-twelve-months EBITDA with accrued interest cover of 1.56x; concentration, with Medicaid at 74.89% and four states at 40.23% of premium revenue; a parent that relies on subsidiary dividends and holds a small part of group cash; and shrinking membership with policy headwinds through 2029.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C2; calculation C8; calculation C9
### Overall credit view

Overall, Molina presents a business profile of adequate scale supported by contract-based government revenue, a maturity profile with no principal due before 2028 and low capital needs, but credit quality is constrained by margins that have collapsed with the medical care ratio, concentration in Medicaid and four states, and a parent that owes all the debt while most cash sits in regulated plans. Cash-flow durability appears weak at present because operating cash flow swings with settlement timing and reported earnings include reserve releases. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on whether the medical care ratio recovers before 2028 and on the coupon needed to replace notes now carrying low rates. The primary downside path is medical costs outrunning premium rates while membership falls. Further analysis would require the credit agreement definitions, the proxy statement, market prices of the notes and management's 2027 plan. Fundamental credit review completed with limitations. Top risk: the medical care ratio.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); calculation C2; calculation C6
